deep.reconstruction:
Context: bundle 'Aether' (optics and wave propagation in an anisotropic medium). The page is the Hamilton–Jacobi treatment of the eikonal (characteristic) equation for a quadratic form, that is, of rays or geodesics of the metric a_{ik}.

(1) The PDE. Riemann sets r = sum_{i,k} alpha_{ik} (ds/dx_i)(ds/dx_k). Here alpha_{ik} is symmetric and is the inverse matrix of a_{ik}; the inverse relation is implicit and is my inference. He takes a complete integral s = f(x_1..x_n, c_1..c_{n-1}) + c_n.

(2) Momentum-velocity change of variables. He defines p_i by r p_i = sum_k alpha_{ik} s_k, where s_k = ds/dx_k. Inverting gives s_i = r sum_k a_{ik} p_k. He writes ds/dx_i = sum_k a_{ik} p_k, which means r = 1, i.e. the equation being solved is sum alpha_{ik} s_i s_k = 1. Generally sum a_{ik} p_i p_k = 1/r, so his normalization sum a_{ik} p_i p_k = 1 is again r = 1.

(3) Characteristic system. He writes
ds : dx_1 : ... : dx_n : 2 d(sum_k a_{hk} p_k) = 1 : p_1 : ... : p_n : sum_{i,k} (da_{ik}/dx_h) p_i p_k.
In modern terms, take H(x,q) = q^T alpha q with q = grad s. Then:
- dx/dt = 2 alpha q = 2p.
- ds/dt = q·dx/dt = 2.
- dq_h/dt = -q^T (d alpha/dx_h) q = p^T (da/dx_h) p.
So dx_i/ds = p_i, and 2 dq_h/ds = sum (da_{ik}/dx_h) p_i p_k. This is exactly the Euler–Lagrange (geodesic) equation of L = sum a_{ik} x'_i x'_k, with arclength s as parameter.

(4) Jacobi's theorem. ds/dc_j = beta_j (j = 1..n-1) with arbitrary constants beta_j give the integral curves (rays). ds/dc_n = 1 holds trivially.

(5) Struck-out attempts, then a clean version. He multiplies the equations I (s_i = sum a_{ik} p_k) by r p_i = sum_h alpha_{ih} s_h and sums. Using sum_i a_{ik} alpha_{ih} = delta_{kh}, he gets sum_i r p_i s_i = sum_{ik} alpha_{ik} s_i s_k = r. Hence sum p_i s_i = 1.

(6) Along a characteristic, ds = sum s_i dx_i = sum a_{ik} p_k dx_i. With dx_i = p_i ds this gives ds = (sum a_{ik} p_i p_k) ds, consistent with the normalization. The following line is the product rule for d(s · sum a p p), written out with d(sum a_{ik} p_i p_k) = sum (da_{ik}/dx_h) p_i p_k dx_h + 2 sum a_{ik} p_k dp_i.

(7) Since sum a p p = 1 is constant: 0 = sum (da_{ik}/dx_h) p_i p_k dx_h + 2 sum a_{ik} p_i dp_k. He treats p as a field p(x) on the family of rays and puts dx_h = p_h ds. This gives
0 = [sum (da_{ik}/dx_h) p_i p_k p_h + 2 sum a_{ik} p_i p_h dp_k/dx_h] ds.
This equals the geodesic equation of (3) contracted with p_h (my check). The page breaks off here.
errors: The relation s_i = sum a_{ik} p_k silently assumes r = 1. In general s_i = r sum a_{ik} p_k and sum a p p = 1/r. Not an error if the equation is the eikonal sum alpha s s = 1, but the normalization is not stated.

In the proportion, the term written '2 sum a_{i,k} dp_k' must be read as 2 d(sum_k a_{hk} p_k), the full differential. If literally sum a_{hk} dp_k, the term sum (da_{hk}/dx_j) p_j p_k is missing and the ray equation would be wrong.
In the product-rule line, the middle term lacks the factor dx_h. Its 'ds' and '·s' placements are sloppy (scratch work).
In the first line after 'Wir multipliciren', the LHS reads sum a_{ik} s_k s_i where sum alpha_{ik} s_i s_k (or sum r p_i s_i) is meant; it is a slip.
The struck-out lines contain an incorrect attempt (r p_i + ...) and were rightly abandoned.

results.what: Hamilton–Jacobi / characteristic system for the quadratic eikonal equation sum alpha_{ik} s_i s_k = 1, with rays dx_i/ds = p_i and 2 d(sum a_{hk}p_k)/ds = sum (da_{ik}/dx_h) p_i p_k
results.modern_name: Characteristics of the eikonal equation = geodesics of the metric a_{ik} (Hamilton's canonical equations, Legendre transform q = a p)

results.what: Complete integral s = f(x,c)+c_n; ds/dc_j = beta_j give the rays
Identities sum p_i s_i = 1 and conservation of sum a_{ik} p_i p_k along rays, with its differential consequence
results.modern_name: Conservation of the Hamiltonian / constant speed of geodesics

deep.surprise_reason: This is standard Hamilton–Jacobi theory applied to a variable quadratic form (rays in an anisotropic or inhomogeneous aether). Riemann's fluency with Jacobi's dynamics and with quadratic forms a_{ik}(x) is well known (1854 Habilitation, 1861 Commentatio). The page contains scratch derivations, not a new result.

checkable.sympy: a11,a12,a22,s1,s2,r=symbols('a11 a12 a22 s1 s2 r'); A=Matrix([[a11,a12],[a12,a22]]); Al=A.inv(); S=Matrix([s1,s2]); P=Al*S/((S.T*Al*S)[0]); simplify((P.T*S)[0]-1)
checkable.asserts: With r = s^T alpha s and p = alpha s / r, sum p_i s_i = 1 identically.
sum a_{ik} p_i p_k = 1/r, so the normalization sum a p p = 1 is equivalent to r = 1.

transcription_corrections: The coefficient in the first line and in the r p_i equations is alpha_{i,k} (drawn like a 'd'), distinct from a_{i,k} in the right-hand column; the transcription is consistent with this.
The opening crossed-out fragment '[-r p_1 x-]' is a false start for 'r p_1'; it is not part of the mathematics.
In the proportion, '2 sum a_{i,k} dp_k' should be read as 2 d(sum_k a_{h,k} p_k), and the last ratio member as sum (da_{i,k}/dx_h) p_i p_k.
In the product-rule line, the second term should carry dx_h; the trailing '·s' factors are part of differentiating sum a p p · s.
In the last line, the struck-out tail '[-p_i p_h ds-]' was apparently intended to be rewritten. The intended expression is 2 sum a_{i,k} (dp_k/dx_h) p_i p_h ds.
